item.title: Fertility Doctor Accused of Using Own Sperm to Impregnate Woman
item.description: Dr. Dennis Lutz, the chairman of the University of North Dakota’s OB-GYN department, did not deny the claims in a lawsuit. The university said it intends to fire him.
item.dc:creator: Mack Liederman
item.media:credit: Education Images/Universal Images Group, via Getty Images
item.media:description: A spokesman for the University of North Dakota said it was taking steps to fire Dr. Dennis Lutz, the chairman of the OB-GYN department.

item.title: Parents of Toddler Found Alive in Arizona Morgue Will Not Face Charges
item.description: The boy, who was 18 months old, had been found unconscious in a pool at the family home in Gilbert, Ariz., and was declared dead. But a medical examiner’s employee later discovered he was breathing.
item.dc:creator: Mark Walker

item.title: Dentists in Brooklyn Exploited Patients in Pain, Lawsuit Charges
item.description: New York City sued two dental practices, saying they offered patients high-interest loans to pay their bills and often falsely said procedures were not covered by insurance.
item.dc:creator: Andy Newman
item.category: Department of Consumer and Worker Protection (NYC)

item.title: Tributes, and Politics Too, at Lindsey Graham’s Funeral in South Carolina
item.description: A gathering of South Carolina’s political elite paid tribute to the late senator’s career against a backdrop of a highly competitive race to replace him.
item.dc:creator: Emily Davies
item.media:description: Mr. Graham’s funeral took place at First Baptist Church of Columbia.

item.title: Clara Ester, Who Was With Martin Luther King Jr. in His Last Moments, Dies at 78
item.description: A Memphis college student and activist, she witnessed Dr. King’s assassination in 1968 when he was shot at his motel and ran to him to check his pulse.
item.dc:creator: Jeré Longman
item.media:credit: Chris Day/The Commercial Appeal, via USA TODAY Network — Reuters Connect
item.media:description: On April 4, 1968, Clara Ester drove to the Lorraine Motel, where the Rev. Dr. Martin Luther King Jr. was shot outside his room.

item.title: U.S. Strikes Iran Again, as Trump Encounters a More Determined Adversary in Widened War
item.description: The United States is again exchanging strikes with Iran, just days after the president appeared to reject plans to escalate.
item.dc:creator: Julian E. Barnes, Helene Cooper and Eric Schmitt
item.category: US and Israeli Attack on Iran (2026)
item.media:description: President Trump in Oakland County Michigan on Monday. The war that President Trump has been trying to bring to a diplomatic conclusion since April is now threatening to grow bigger.

item.title: Record Numbers of FOIA Public Document Requests Are in Limbo or Unfulfilled

item.title: Trump Has Made Billions in Office. Will His Party Pay Politically?
item.description: The president took in a staggering $2.2 billion last year while in office. Democrats are hoping to make it a campaign issue in the midterm elections.

item.title: Trump Unveils $22.5 Billion Redesign of Dulles Airport

item.title: Families Face Anxiety, Angst as Loved Ones Are Deployed to Fight Iran
item.description: As the war with Iran has continued, some are finding that the stress is bringing back old anxieties.
item.dc:creator: Bernard Mokam and Georgia Gee
item.category: United States Defense and Military Forces
US and Israeli Attack on Iran (2026)
item.media:description: Mental health counselors say they are attending to more military families who are reporting stress and anxiety about a conflict that has taken the lives of at least 18 service members and wounded more than 400.

item.title: 10 Women Accuse Jared Leto of Sexual Misconduct in BBC Report
item.description: The accusations include sex with underage girls and sexually explicit messages. The actor denied the allegations.
item.dc:creator: Remy Tumin

item.title: Fauci’s Pardon From Biden Would Not Shield Him From New Offenses
item.description: Republicans have argued that the pre-emptive pardon Dr. Fauci received from former President Biden ought to preclude him from invoking the Fifth Amendment. But the pardon applies only to what happened before it was issued.
item.dc:creator: Karoun Demirjian
item.media:credit: Stefani Reynolds for The New York Times
item.media:description: Former President Joseph R. Biden Jr. and Dr. Anthony S. Fauci during a news conference at the White House in 2021. Mr. Biden issued a pre-emptive pardon for Dr. Fauci on the last day of his term as president.

item.title: Teenage Lifeguard Fights Intense Waves to Bring Boy to Safety
item.description: A lifeguard with a relentless grip on a young boy brought him to safety amid enormous waves that ripped across a Santa Cruz beach over the weekend.
item.dc:creator: Sejal Govindarao and Pooja Salhotra

item.title: Senators Cornyn and Tillis Force Delay of Blanche Nomination Over Trump’s IRS Deal
item.description: John Cornyn and Thom Tillis accused the nominee for attorney general of refusing to put on paper his promise to kill aspects of the deal he cut to settle President Trump’s suit against the agency.
item.dc:creator: Glenn Thrush and Michael Gold
item.media:description: Todd Blanche, the acting attorney general, cannot afford to lose a single Republican vote.

item.title: Lindsay Clancy Trial Update: In 911 Call, Husband Screams, ‘She Killed the Kids’
item.description: Prosecutors say Lindsay Clancy planned the killings of her three young children. Her lawyers point to her severe postpartum mental illness.
item.dc:creator: Jenna Russell
item.media:description: Patrick Clancy, testifying in court on Monday in Plymouth, Mass. On Tuesday, his voice was barely audible at times.

item.title: Sanctions Bill Would Give Trump Sweeping New Tariff Powers
item.description: A bipartisan bill in the Senate would allow President Trump to impose tariffs on the biggest importers of Russian energy.
item.dc:creator: Alan Rappeport
item.media:description: The president has expressed a preference for using tariffs over sanctions as an economic weapon.

item.title: Florida Professor Fired for Assigning a Profane Story, Lawsuit Says
item.description: South Florida State College fired an English professor after she assigned a story about a teacher who talks about sex with her students. Now the professor is suing.
item.dc:creator: David Ovalle
item.category: Foundation for Individual Rights and Expression (Nonprofit)
item.media:credit: Jacob Langston for The New York Times
item.media:description: Vinita Prabhakar, who taught English at South Florida State College, said in an interview that she assigned the story to challenge her students.

item.title: With Blanche Nomination at Stake, Payouts to Trump Allies Continue
item.description: A seven-figure settlement was announced hours before senators skeptical about the so-called weaponization fund delayed a crucial vote on Todd Blanche’s nomination to be attorney general.
item.dc:creator: Devlin Barrett and Alan Feuer
item.media:description: Todd Blanche, the acting attorney general, has said the Justice Department dropped its plan for a $1.8 billion fund to pay purported victims of government weaponization, but the department can make such payouts even without a formal fund structure.
